figure: Figure 8.1 — Where inference computation and data movement actually live

acceptance_test: Separate compute units from the memory hierarchy (e.g., place tensor cores/ALU in a side column or annotate them as execution resources), and make the capacity/speed/distance gradient apply only to storage levels. A reader should be able to state correctly that tensor cores are compute, not storage.

figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The subtitle's '140 GB: NVLink 544 ms | HDR 6,125 ms | RoCE 98,000 ms' is ambiguous about what the 140 GB denotes. acceptance_test: Revise the subtitle to say '140 GB logical tensor per rank (245 GB sent/rank): NVLink 544 ms | HDR 6,125 ms | RoCE 98,000 ms' or equivalent, so the 140 GB quantity is explicitly tied to the x-axis and the 1.75× multiplier is visible at the point of use.

acceptance_test: Either (a) route the dashed setup path through the framework-backend boxes (launcher/rendezvous → ProcessGroupNCCL/XCCL → NCCL/oneCCL), or (b) add an explicit note in the figure or caption that the dashed path represents only the bootstrap/unique-ID distribution and that the framework backend still participates in communicator creation. evidence: Figure label: 'BEFORE: naive / SDPA'; caption: 'Before (naive / SDPA), the intermediate attention matrix is materialized to HBM and re-read'; page 227 text defines SDPA as 'Scaled-dot-product attention (SDPA)' and discusses FlashAttention as an implementation of the same math.
